subject: science
chapter_title: Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet

concepts.title: Why Earth Is a Unique Planet
concepts.definition: Among all known worlds, earth alone hosts life: it sits at the right distance from the sun, holds water in all three states, and is wrapped in a breathable atmosphere - a rare combination that makes it our one known home.
concepts.key_idea: Right distance, right temperature, liquid water and a friendly atmosphere make earth unique.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu113.txt lines 48-111 (why is earth a unique planet)
question_patterns: why is the earth called a unique planet
which conditions make life possible on earth
why can life not exist on most other planets
what is special about the earth's distance from the sun
compare the earth with its neighbouring planets
list three features that only the earth shows

solution_steps.explain: Earth orbits in the habitable zone where water stays liquid.
Its atmosphere traps just enough heat and supplies oxygen.
No other explored world combines these life-friendly conditions.

concepts.title: The Planets of the Solar System
concepts.definition: Eight planets travel around the sun in order - Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune; the inner four are small rocky worlds while the outer ones are gas and ice giants, each differing in size, distance, moons and temperature.
concepts.key_idea: Rocky near, gaseous far: the solar system divides into terrestrial and giant planets.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu113.txt lines 111-213 (planets of our solar system)
question_patterns: name the planets of the solar system in order from the sun
which planets are called gas giants

distinguish terrestrial planets from outer giants

solution_steps.explain: List the eight planets outward from the sun.
Mercury to Mars are rocky; Jupiter outward are gas and ice giants.
Distance, atmosphere and size set each planet's temperature and weather.

concepts.title: What Makes Earth Suitable for Life
concepts.definition: Life on earth rests on a supporting trio: liquid water covering most of the surface, an atmosphere with oxygen and a protective ozone layer, and a temperature range kept steady by the greenhouse effect and the planet's spin and tilt.
concepts.key_idea: Water, oxygen-rich air and moderate temperatures are the three pillars of earthly life.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu113.txt lines 213-362 (what makes the earth suitable for life)
question_patterns: which factors make the earth suitable for life
why is liquid water essential for living beings
how does the atmosphere protect life on earth
what is the role of the ozone layer
how does the greenhouse effect help life on earth
why is a moderate temperature range important for survival

solution_steps.explain: Liquid water dissolves and transports substances for every living cell.
Oxygen supports respiration while the ozone layer screens harmful ultraviolet rays.
A balanced greenhouse keeps temperatures inside the living range.

concepts.title: Sustaining Life: Cycles and Shields
concepts.definition: Earth keeps life running through endless cycles - water, oxygen, carbon and nitrogen circulate between air, soil and living things - while gravity holds the atmosphere and the magnetic field deflects harmful solar wind.
concepts.key_idea: Recycling cycles and planetary shields keep the biosphere running without a break.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu113.txt lines 362-460 (what allows life to be sustained on earth)
question_patterns: how do the water and oxygen cycles sustain life
what is the role of the nitrogen cycle
how does the magnetic field protect life on earth
why is gravity important for holding the atmosphere
explain how carbon cycles between air and living things
name the cycles that keep matter moving in the biosphere

solution_steps.explain: Water evaporates, rains and flows; oxygen and carbon pass between respiration and photosynthesis.
Gravity keeps the air; the magnetic field turns away charged solar particles.
Endless recycling of matter and steady energy from the sun sustain life.

concepts.title: Threats to Life on Earth
concepts.definition: Human activity now strains the life-support system: pollution of air and water, climate change from excess greenhouse gases, ozone depletion, deforestation and careless resource use all weaken the planet's ability to keep sustaining life.
concepts.key_idea: Pollution and warming chip away at the very conditions that make earth livable.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu113.txt lines 656-740 (threats to life on earth)
question_patterns: list the major threats to life on earth today
how does air pollution harm living beings
what causes climate change and why is it dangerous
how does deforestation disturb the water cycle
why is ozone depletion a threat to life
suggest steps to reduce threats to the earth's environment

solution_steps.explain: Pollution, warming, ozone holes and habitat loss top the list.
Each threat weakens water, air or temperature conditions that life needs.
Saving energy, planting trees and cutting waste ease the pressure.
